title: Finite intrinsic projection proper factor
statement: Fix D,C,E,m,S,f,c,K,L,U,V,k,l as in [def-sf-finite-intrinsic-projection-coordinates], with the specified canonical comparison [def-sf-canonical-finite-intrinsic-tensor-comparison]. The proper factor satisfies the intrinsic proper factor followed by midpoint equals the canonical source-coordinate maps followed by sourceComparison.hom and fixedProper. This compares only the actual proper counit mate; no open projection or pullback compositor occurs.

source.place: Every step constructs or compares the same projection map; finite constant-coefficient realization, proper counit and open tensor factors.

proof.text: apply the inverse coefficient equivalence at the output, and then the Hom bijection of the fixed inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. The intrinsic proper factor transposes to the finite tensor/pullback comparison followed by the actual counit tensored with identity. The finite scalar tensor realization is induced by the ordinary balanced tensor comparison on simultaneous flat K-flat representatives. On those representatives its square with inverse image sends a pure tensor to the same two pulled-back sections. Descend that square through the two localization functors. The section-normalized inverse-image comparison identifies the actual units, hence the counits, of the intrinsic and fixed adjunctions. Substitute this counit equation in the transposed square; tensor naturality moves k and l to the endpoints. The direct-image realization comparison is normalized on K-injective representatives, so the resulting target comparison is exactly midpoint. Expand sourceComparison and supportRealization: inverse finiteSupport cancels finiteSupport, and the open coefficient unit cancels with the open realization in midpoint. The coefficient triangle identities cancel the remaining inner units. Adjunction injectivity and faithfulness of the coefficient equivalence give the equation. No invertibility of the proper projection is used. Zero inputs, empty schemes and m=0 satisfy the same unit and representative equations.

theorem finiteIntrinsicProjectionProperFactor
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] (m : ℕ)
    (S : SixFunctorFiniteOperations D C E (m + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 m))
    {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : Compactification f.hom.left)
    (K : sixFunctorFiniteCategory D C E (m + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 m) X)
    (L : finiteTorConstructibleCategory C.l E (m + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 m) Y.obj.left)
    (U : normalizedDVRDerived C.l E X.obj.left m)
    (V : normalizedDVRDerived C.l E Y.obj.left m) (k : U ≅ K.obj) (l : V ≅ L.obj) :
    (SystemProjectionFormula.finiteProperProjection C.l E D C.different c.g
      (c.g ≫ Y.obj.hom) Y.obj.hom m
      (((sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero c.i
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E (m + 1))).mapDerivedCategory).obj U) V) ≫
        midpoint m f c K L U V k l =
      ((canonicalFiniteIntrinsicTensorComparison (C := C) (E := E) m Y).hom.app
        ((sixFunctorFiniteSupport D C E (m + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 m) f c).obj U, V) ≫
        (evaluatedTensor (C := C) (E := E) m Y).map
          (Prod.mkHom ((sixFunctorFiniteSupport D C E (m + 1)
            (Nat.le_add_left 1 m) f c).map k.hom ≫
              (S.finiteSupport f c).inv.app K) l.hom)) ≫
        (sourceComparison S f c K L).hom ≫ fixedProper m f c K L
